coverage_model.entry_point_rule: Every one of the 96 unique inherent or declared public methods from K0.1 appears exactly once across configuration_fields, enum_semantics, and operations. KPR-OP-001 additionally freezes the three reachable KafkaError trait operations Display::fmt, Error::source, and From<io::Error>::from, which K0.1 public_methods did not enumerate. For a configuration row, surface is the exact field access path; a private field also names at least one public writer in public_entry_points. The coverage receipt pins the exact reviewed entry-point to semantic-row/source-owner/source-anchor map, the source-owner/source-anchor map for all 97 semantic rows, and each source-pin identity/path/count/hash/role mapping. The contract checks a matching function declaration boundary inside every public-entry anchor and pins the complete artifact and companion-document bytes.
coverage_model.field_rule: Every field in ProducerConfig, KafkaTlsConfig, KafkaSaslConfig, TransactionalConfig, and ConsumerConfig has exactly one stable row. Public fields are direct entry points even when no dedicated builder exists.

shared_semantics.manual_commit_default: ConsumerConfig.enable_auto_commit defaults false. Poll does not store or commit an offset in that default mode; the caller passes the next-to-read offset to commit_offsets after processing.
shared_semantics.auto_commit_opt_in: On the real-broker path, enabling auto commit leaves enable.auto.offset.store=false but poll stores the message offset before returning the record; librdkafka later flushes it. A commit before application completion creates a loss window, while a crash before the delayed commit can still redeliver. The deterministic path ignores enable_auto_commit: poll advances only positions, never committed_offsets, and has no background commit.
shared_semantics.idempotence: ProducerConfig defaults enable_idempotence=true. The transactional client forces broker enable.idempotence=true even when the retained public producer config says false; deterministic paths do not deduplicate.
shared_semantics.caller_driven_rebalance: KafkaConsumer::rebalance is an explicit assign or unassign operation supplied by the caller. The source contains no real ConsumerContext rebalance callback lifecycle.
shared_semantics.remote_plaintext_policy: Plaintext host extraction trims the extracted host; a leading [ selects text through the first ] and ignores any suffix, otherwise the last : splits host from an unchecked suffix. The exact accepted hosts are ASCII-case-insensitive localhost, any IPv4 loopback, ::1, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 only when its mapped IPv4 is loopback. Missing ], non-loopback or unparseable hosts fail; no port/endpoint grammar is otherwise enforced. TLS, SASL_SSL, or the private bypass skip the host rejection. The public bypass setter exists under test or debug_assertions, so downstream debug builds can call it.
shared_semantics.secret_redaction: SASL passwords use a private ZeroizeOnDrop wrapper and Debug redaction. TLS key passwords are private and Debug-redacted but stored in ordinary cloneable String storage without zeroization. Authentication error strings are not sanitized. Native ClientConfig failures can return a rejected value; producer mapping, consumer mapping, and KafkaClient error formatting expose that value without redaction, including a possible sasl.password or ssl.key.password.
shared_semantics.no_feature_lane: Public configuration and facade types remain compiled except for the row-specific test/debug-gated admission fields and setters. Valid optional producer and transaction constructors can create local objects, but ordinary downstream broker operations fail with FeatureDisabled. KafkaProducer send, TransactionalProducer begin, and primary-consumer backend operations require crate tests or their explicit test-internals config admission. After begin returns a Transaction handle, send, commit, abort, and drop do not recheck producer admission. In release test-internals, only operations that reach the process-global deterministic broker panic guard fail that way; transaction begin, staging, abort, drop, and several consumer local-state operations do not touch that guard. The parallel KafkaClient consumer remains asymmetric.
shared_semantics.error_taxonomy: Producer/transaction mapping is exact: ClientConfig maps to Config(value); MessageProduction QueueFull maps to QueueFull, InvalidTopic or UnknownTopic maps to InvalidTopic(message topic or `unknown`), and every other production code maps to Broker(Debug code); Canceled maps to Cancelled; every other error maps to Authentication only when Display contains one of `Authentication`, `SASL`, `authentication`, `Invalid credentials`, `Broker: Authentication failed`, `SASL_PLAINTEXT`, or `SASL_SSL`, otherwise Broker(Display). Primary-consumer mapping is exact: Canceled maps to Cancelled; ClientConfig maps to Config containing desc, key, and value; ClientCreation or Subscription maps to Config(message); every other error maps to Broker(Display). Only Io(TimedOut) is_timeout; no stable ASUP-Exxx token is emitted by primary Kafka operations.
shared_semantics.cancellation_model: Cx-aware operations check at entry. Poll and retry backoff recheck while waiting; blocking broker calls and already-enqueued delivery are not interrupted, so some completion outcomes remain ambiguous.
shared_semantics.shutdown_model: KafkaProducer close marks closed before flush. KafkaConsumer close marks closed before backend cleanup and cannot retry cleanup after a partial failure. TransactionalProducer has no explicit close operation; unfinished transaction drop defers broker abort until a later begin.
shared_semantics.resource_model: Local configuration string/count limits are mostly absent. Producer caps payload bytes only. Consumer copies one returned record and its headers without local payload/header limits; max_poll_records is inert. Deterministic topic and staged-record vectors have no aggregate cap.
shared_semantics.observability_model: Primary Kafka operations expose string errors and local diagnostic accessors but no stable error-code registry tokens and no complete metrics or tracing contract. In debug/test deterministic single-record send, a case-sensitive critical-topic match writes exactly WARNING: publishing to critical topic '{topic}' using deterministic Kafka harness. This is safe only in test environments. to stderr. Deterministic transaction batch commit bypasses the critical-topic matcher and emits no per-topic warning.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: Ordinary configuration types, fields, defaults, builders, and synchronous validation remain compiled. KPR-CFG-013 and KCO-CFG-017 setters require test or debug_assertions; KPR-CFG-014 and KCO-CFG-018 fields and setters require test or test-internals. Reading or writing any compiled value performs no broker access.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: The same stored values and local validation apply. Outside crate tests the producer admission field gates KafkaProducer send and transaction begin, while the consumer admission field gates primary-consumer backend operations. Operations on an existing Transaction handle do not recheck producer admission.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: Configuration access and mutation do not reach process-global deterministic storage and therefore do not trigger its release guard. A later operation may do so as specified by its own profile group.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: All listed enums and their ordinary methods remain compiled and are pure local values; their broker mappings are dormant until used by an operation.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: Enum values and local conversions retain the same source-defined behavior; deterministic paths may ignore native-only mappings such as compression and isolation.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: Enum construction and inspection are local and never enter deterministic global storage.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: Error classifiers, producer and consumer validation, and TopicPartitionOffset construction execute locally with the same accepted and rejected values.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: These operations remain pure local classification, validation, or value construction and do not consult deterministic broker state.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: These operations do not touch deterministic global storage and cannot trigger its release guard.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: A Required producer configuration returns FeatureDisabled; an Optional valid configuration constructs a local producer whose later backend operations remain profile-dependent.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: Crate-test and test-internals construction both succeed without reading the admission flag or accessing global storage. Outside crate tests, explicit admission is checked later by KafkaProducer send.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: Explicitly admitted construction succeeds locally and does not itself touch deterministic global storage.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: An ordinarily constructed Optional producer returns FeatureDisabled before deterministic publication.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: Crate-test admission, or explicit debug test-internals admission, copies and publishes the record into process-global deterministic storage and returns the exact local metadata frozen in KPR-OP-004. A case-sensitive critical-topic match writes the exact KPR-OP-004 warning to stderr before publication.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: An explicitly admitted valid critical-topic send reaches the topic-specific panic before the general storage guard; a noncritical send reaches the distinct general guard. Neither panic is returned as KafkaError.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: Flush observes only the local active-operation count, close performs the same local closed-state transition and drain, and both accessors remain available on an Optional no-feature producer.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: These lifecycle and accessor operations use local counters, flags, and retained configuration; deterministic sends have already completed synchronously before they drain.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: These operations do not directly access deterministic global storage. They retain their local success, cancellation, poll-slice-budget, and closed-state outcomes.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: A Required transactional configuration fails construction, while an Optional one constructs locally. Outside crate tests, begin returns FeatureDisabled unless the producer admission flag is true; therefore abort and unfinished-active-handle drop are unreachable through the ordinary public no-feature API. Accessors remain local.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: Crate tests admit begin automatically; outside crate tests explicit producer admission is required. After begin activates the phase, abort clears local staged records without rechecking admission, and dropping an unfinished handle marks NeedsAbortRecovery without an immediate broker abort.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: Construction and accessors remain local; explicitly admitted begin also avoids global storage. After a handle exists, abort and drop do not recheck admission or touch global storage, including entry-cancellation poisoning of a consumed abort handle.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: No active Transaction handle is reachable through the ordinary public no-feature API because begin requires admission. The separately compiled send branch would return FeatureDisabled if reached; that branch is UNREACHABLE_FROM_PUBLIC_API in this profile.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: After crate-test automatic admission or an explicitly admitted test-internals begin, an active transaction copies the record into its local unbounded staged vector without rechecking the producer admission flag; no process-global broker access occurs until commit.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: After an explicitly admitted begin, transaction send succeeds by staging locally without rechecking the producer admission flag and does not trigger the deterministic broker release guard.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: No active Transaction handle is reachable through the ordinary public no-feature API because begin requires admission. The separately compiled commit branch would mark Idle and finished then return FeatureDisabled; that branch is UNREACHABLE_FROM_PUBLIC_API in this profile.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: After crate-test automatic admission or an explicitly admitted test-internals begin, commit takes the full staged vector without rechecking the producer admission flag, publishes it atomically under the local broker lock, marks Idle, and finishes the consuming handle. Batch publication bypasses the single-record critical-topic matcher and emits no per-topic warning.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: After an explicitly admitted begin, an empty commit returns normally because publication exits before global storage. A nonempty commit moves to Finalizing, takes staged records, then panics at the release guard; unwinding drops the unfinished handle and leaves NeedsAbortRecovery. Commit does not recheck the producer admission flag.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: Backend and consumer-trait descriptors, KafkaClient construction with a valid Optional producer configuration, and producer/backend accessors remain local; construction does not inspect deterministic admission, and descriptors do not prove broker availability.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: The same diagnostics and accessors expose the locally selected deterministic backend and producer without reading global broker storage.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: These descriptor, construction, and accessor operations do not touch deterministic global storage.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: Outside crate tests KafkaClient::consumer returns InvalidTopic for an empty or whitespace-only topic; after successful topic validation it returns FeatureDisabled even though its backend descriptor says deterministic.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: Only the crate-test cfg branch constructs and caches the one-topic DeterministicConsumer diagnostics object; test-internals alone does not enable that branch.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: Because release test-internals is not cfg(test), KafkaClient::consumer returns InvalidTopic for an invalid topic or FeatureDisabled after successful topic validation and never reaches deterministic global storage.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: Every valid ConsumerConfig constructs a local consumer object; ordinary backend-directed operations fail later when deterministic broker operations are not admitted.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: A no-feature crate test constructs the deterministic consumer automatically. With the kafka feature under cfg(test), force_real_kafka=false constructs a unit-local consumer with no BaseConsumer and no deterministic record store, while true constructs the real backend. A no-feature debug test-internals build constructs locally and checks explicit admission at later backend-directed operations.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: Construction moves the config into local state and does not access deterministic global storage.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: Subscribe, caller-driven rebalance, explicit commit, and seek return FeatureDisabled before mutating backend-dependent state when deterministic operations are not admitted.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: In no-feature crate tests or explicitly admitted no-feature debug test-internals, these operations update local subscription, assignment, commit-cache, and position state without process-global record storage. A kafka-feature crate test with force_real_kafka=false uses the same unit-local state path; true delegates to the real backend.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: In a no-feature release test-internals build with explicit admission these operations remain local and do not trigger the deterministic broker release guard. With the kafka feature they use the real backend path.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: Poll returns FeatureDisabled before subscription or record access when deterministic operations are not admitted.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: In a no-feature crate test or explicitly admitted no-feature debug test-internals build, poll can return Config during local position initialization or Ok(None) for an empty assignment and zero timeout before storage access. When it enters the deterministic read/wait path, it reads process-global storage, round-robins assignments, copies at most one record, ignores enable_auto_commit, advances only positions, and performs no background commit. With the kafka feature under cfg(test), force_real_kafka=false uses the feature-on unit-local wait path and never reads deterministic records; true polls the real backend.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: In a no-feature release test-internals build, an explicitly admitted poll that enters the deterministic read/wait path reaches the broker accessor and triggers the release guard. With the kafka feature it uses the real backend path.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: Close and every listed accessor operate on local consumer state; close succeeds and clears its listed maps even when backend-directed operations were unavailable.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: These operations read or clear local state and do not fetch deterministic records; close notifies local waiters.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: These local close and accessor operations do not touch deterministic global storage and do not trigger its release guard.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: These helpers are absent from an ordinary downstream build without test or test-internals cfg admission.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: End-offset reads initialized deterministic storage. Reset clears only an already initialized broker, and lock acquires the separate test lock then resets; reset and lock do not themselves initialize the broker.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: End-offset calls the guarded broker accessor and panics. Reset and lock have no direct guard call while the broker remains uninitialized, although reset can mutate already initialized state.

profile_disposition_groups.no_feature_behavior: These conversion and parser-scaffolding helpers are absent unless test, cfg(fuzzing), or the fuzz feature admits them; they are not ordinary production Kafka operations.
profile_disposition_groups.deterministic_behavior: When compiled, every helper operates only on supplied bytes or values and never accesses deterministic broker state.
profile_disposition_groups.release_test_internals_behavior: Test-internals alone does not compile these helpers, and any independently admitted fuzz profile remains local and does not access deterministic broker storage.

configuration_fields.cfg_visibility: native; public field and public constructor
configuration_fields.accepted_values: Any nonempty vector whose effective security policy accepts every endpoint. Plaintext host extraction trims the host, treats bracketed text through the first ] as the host while ignoring any suffix, otherwise splits at the last :, and accepts ASCII-case-insensitive localhost, any IPv4 loopback, ::1, or IPv4-mapped IPv6 whose mapped IPv4 is loopback. TLS/SASL or bypassed Plaintext skips this classifier and accepts empty, malformed, duplicated, or arbitrarily long entries.
configuration_fields.rejected_values: Empty vector; without bypass, any Plaintext entry whose extracted host is not one of the exact loopback forms, including a leading [ without a closing ], a non-loopback mapped IPv6, or an unparseable hostname. No port or endpoint grammar is otherwise enforced.
configuration_fields.broker_mapping: Entries are comma-joined into bootstrap.servers.
configuration_fields.success_outcome: The constructor stores the vector; producer construction validates it.
configuration_fields.error_outcome: Config for empty or rejected remote plaintext; a Required no-feature config yields FeatureDisabled first.
configuration_fields.shutdown_rule: Copied into producer and transaction client configuration; no clearing rule.
configuration_fields.credential_payload_rule: Endpoint text is retained and can appear in a Config error; it is not treated as a secret.

operations.success_outcome: Classifier truth sets are exact: transient is Io, Broker, QueueFull, or Transaction; connection is Io or Broker; capacity is QueueFull or MessageTooLarge; timeout is only Io(TimedOut); retryable is Io, Broker, or QueueFull. Display templates are exact: Io -> 'Kafka I/O error: {source}'; Protocol -> 'Kafka protocol error: {message}'; Broker -> 'Kafka broker error: {message}'; QueueFull -> 'Kafka producer queue is full'; MessageTooLarge -> 'Kafka message too large: {size} bytes (max: {max_size})'; InvalidTopic -> 'Invalid Kafka topic: {topic}'; Transaction -> 'Kafka transaction error: {message}'; Cancelled -> 'Kafka operation cancelled'; PolledAfterCompletion -> 'Kafka future polled after completion'; Config -> 'Kafka configuration error: {message}'; Authentication -> 'Kafka authentication failed: {message}'; FeatureDisabled -> 'Kafka is unavailable: the `kafka` cargo feature is not enabled in this build'. Error::source returns Some only for Io and None for every other variant. From<io::Error> preserves the supplied error inside Io.

operations.default: Legal from Idle; first use attempts native initialization, but the check-await-set sequence is not serialized across concurrent begin calls.
operations.accepted_values: Open logical state Idle, including successful recovery from NeedsAbortRecovery; outside crate tests in a no-feature test-internals build, the producer deterministic-broker admission flag must be true.
operations.rejected_values: Active, Finalizing, unrecovered poisoned state, native init/recovery/begin failure, or no-feature operation outside crate tests without the producer deterministic-broker admission flag.
operations.broker_mapping: May call abort_transaction for recovery, init_transactions, then begin_transaction. Concurrent Idle begins can duplicate native initialization before one local activation rejects. From NeedsAbortRecovery, two callers can both start abort recovery; a later recovery completion can mark Idle after the other caller activated, so both can activate and reach native begin.
operations.success_outcome: A single successful recovery/initialization activates and returns a borrowing Transaction handle. Under the NeedsAbortRecovery race, two calls can both return handles because one recovery completion can clobber the other's Active phase before activating again.
operations.error_outcome: Cancelled at entry; FeatureDisabled for failed no-feature admission; Transaction or mapped Broker errors. Begin failure resets Idle; recovery failure retains NeedsAbortRecovery. In the concurrent recovery race, a later failure can reset Idle while another active handle still exists. If a selected blocking pool rejects enqueue during shutdown, the bridge panics `blocking operation ended without producing a result`: during recovery this leaves NeedsAbortRecovery, during initialization it leaves Idle/uninitialized, and during native begin it occurs after activation and strands Active with no handle or Drop hook. A native-closure panic has the same phase-specific consequences. Spawned closure panics are resumed by the bridge and inline fallback propagates directly. Dropping begin in the same post-activation/pre-handle window has the stranded-Active risk.
operations.retry_rule: No automatic retry; a later begin is the only recovery trigger.
operations.timeout_rule: Configured transaction_timeout applies to recovery abort and initialization only after each native closure begins; configured-pool queueing and fallback-slot waiting are not charged and have no caller deadline. Native begin_transaction itself takes no timeout. If pool worker creation fails with no live worker, an accepted recovery or initialization task can remain queued indefinitely before its timeout starts, and native begin can remain queued indefinitely with no caller timeout at all.
operations.cancellation_rule: Cx is checked before blocking work, but phase is set Active before native begin is awaited and the Transaction handle is constructed only afterward. Dropping the future in that window can cancel queued pool work or discard a running/fallback result while leaving shared phase Active with no handle to poison it; later begin returns transaction already active. With a configured pool, dropping the await cancels the task handle: queued work is skipped, while executing work runs to completion and its result is discarded. On the no-pool fallback, cap saturation yields without consulting this operation Cx, and dropping the await discards the result without stopping an already-started closure.
operations.shutdown_rule: No closed state; unfinished prior handle may require recovery, while cancellation before handle construction can strand Active with no recovery hook.
operations.resource_bound: State checks are locked but native work occurs after releasing the lock; concurrent calls can duplicate blocking native init/recovery work and recovery can admit multiple handles. A configured Cx pool caps worker concurrency at its configured/live maximum but admits pending tasks into an uncapped SegQueue; after worker-spawn failure an accepted task can remain retained indefinitely when no worker is live. Without a pool, the shared fallback counter caps successfully spawned blocking threads at 256 while excess callers wait, and OS-thread spawn failure runs the blocking closure inline on the async worker.
operations.credential_payload_rule: No record content; native errors retain strings.

operations.default: Native and deterministic commit branches move Active to Finalizing before commit; the ordinary no-feature branch moves directly to Idle while returning FeatureDisabled; the handle is consumed.
operations.accepted_values: Active transaction after entry checkpoint.

The compiled ordinary no-feature branch returns FeatureDisabled, but no active handle is publicly reachable there because begin requires admission; an existing handle does not recheck the flag.
operations.broker_mapping: Native commit_transaction with configured timeout; deterministic commit publishes the entire staged vector atomically under the local broker lock. With duplicate handles, ensure-active and mark-finalizing are separate locks, so two callers that both pass the first check can both enter native commit, native abort, or mixed finalization; a separately checked native send can also enqueue or finish during/after finalization. Deterministic commit rechecks atomically and rejects a finalization loser, while deterministic send separately rechecks Active before staging.
operations.success_outcome: Phase returns Idle and handle is marked finished. Debug/test deterministic batch publication does not call the single-record critical-topic matcher and emits no per-topic stderr warning.
operations.error_outcome: Native failure marks NeedsAbortRecovery. Consuming handle prevents retry and no typed ambiguous outcome exists. Duplicate native handles can both finalize; deterministic commit rejects the second after its earlier ensure-active succeeded, and that unfinished loser's Drop can change the winner's Finalizing phase to NeedsAbortRecovery. If a selected blocking pool rejects enqueue during shutdown, the bridge panics `blocking operation ended without producing a result`. Any native-closure panic is resumed (or propagated directly by inline fallback); handle unwinding poisons Finalizing to NeedsAbortRecovery. In release test-internals an empty staged commit succeeds locally, while a nonempty staged commit panics when publication reaches the global deterministic broker guard.
operations.timeout_rule: transaction_timeout begins only when the native closure executes; configured-pool queueing and fallback-slot waiting are not charged, so total future wall time is unbounded. If pool worker creation fails with no live worker, the accepted task can remain queued indefinitely. Timeout classification may be lost in Broker string mapping.
operations.cancellation_rule: Entry cancellation triggers unfinished-drop poisoning; blocking commit does not observe later Cx cancellation. With a configured pool, dropping the await cancels queued work but executing work continues and discards its result. On the no-pool fallback, cap saturation yields without consulting this operation Cx and a dropped await does not stop an already-started closure. Deterministic commit synchronously waits for and holds the process-global broker mutex after its entry checkpoint; neither lock wait nor batch publication observes Cx.
operations.shutdown_rule: Failure requires a later begin to attempt abort recovery; if never reused there is no explicit cleanup.
operations.resource_bound: Deterministic commit takes and publishes an unbounded staged vector while holding the process-global broker mutex for work proportional to record count, topic/key/payload/header bytes, map allocations, and metadata output. Native commit prefers the configured Cx pool, whose worker concurrency is capped but whose pending SegQueue is uncapped; after worker-spawn failure an accepted task can remain retained indefinitely when no worker is live. Without a pool, the shared fallback counter caps successfully spawned blocking threads at 256 while excess callers wait, and OS-thread spawn failure runs the blocking closure inline on the async worker.
operations.credential_payload_rule: Deterministic records are copied into global storage; no durability, replication, fencing, or deduplication.

operations.default: Native abort moves Active to Finalizing before the dependency call; every no-feature abort branch moves directly Active to Idle; the handle is consumed.

operations.broker_mapping: Native abort_transaction with configured timeout; every no-feature branch marks the transaction idle and clears staged local records without touching the global deterministic broker. With duplicate handles, ensure-active and mark-finalizing are separate locks, so two callers that both pass the first check can both enter native abort, native commit, or mixed finalization; a separately checked native send can also enqueue or finish during/after finalization, whereas deterministic send rechecks Active under its staging lock.
operations.success_outcome: Phase returns Idle and handle is marked finished.

If a selected blocking pool rejects enqueue during shutdown, the bridge panics `blocking operation ended without producing a result`. Any native-closure panic is resumed (or propagated directly by inline fallback); handle unwinding poisons Finalizing to NeedsAbortRecovery. After an admitted begin, no-feature abort succeeds locally and does not return FeatureDisabled.

operations.timeout_rule: transaction_timeout begins only when the native closure executes; configured-pool queueing and fallback-slot waiting are not charged, so total future wall time is unbounded. If pool worker creation fails with no live worker, the accepted task can remain queued indefinitely.
operations.cancellation_rule: Entry checkpoint only; because the handle is consumed, entry cancellation drops the unfinished handle and marks NeedsAbortRecovery. Blocking native abort does not observe later cancellation. With a configured pool, dropping the await cancels queued work but executing work continues and discards its result. On the no-pool fallback, cap saturation yields without consulting this operation Cx and a dropped await does not stop an already-started closure.

Native abort prefers the configured Cx pool, whose worker concurrency is capped but whose pending SegQueue is uncapped; after worker-spawn failure an accepted task can remain retained indefinitely when no worker is live. Without a pool, the shared fallback counter caps successfully spawned blocking threads at 256 while excess callers wait, and OS-thread spawn failure runs the blocking closure inline on the async worker.

operations.cfg_visibility: native public async method with cfg-selected backend
operations.default: Manual commit; one optional record; caller-supplied timeout.
operations.accepted_values: Every Duration while open and subscribed.
operations.rejected_values: Entry/inter-slice cancellation, closed or unsubscribed state, backend error, unavailable no-feature backend, or deterministic reset error.
operations.broker_mapping: Serialized BaseConsumer::poll in at most 50ms blocking slices, plus assignment/position snapshot. Deterministic mode sorts local assignments, starts at retained poll_cursor modulo the current assignment count, advances that cursor with wrapping addition, ignores enable_auto_commit, and never updates committed_offsets automatically.
operations.success_outcome: Ok(Some(one owned record)) or Ok(None) on timeout/no message/partition EOF. A real snapshot updates position only for nonnegative absolute Offset values; other offset forms and negative values are dropped, so apply_broker_snapshot can preserve an absent or stale position. Only the real-broker auto-commit opt-in stores before return; deterministic poll advances position without any automatic commit. A real poll can consume a message and then discard it if offset storage or snapshot capture fails; auto-store may already have succeeded before the snapshot error. Because the real path shares one buffered_outcome slot, a later poll can receive a record/snapshot produced for a cancelled or expired earlier call. A newer subscribe/rebalance can complete locally before an older buffered snapshot is consumed; applying that stale snapshot can restore old assignments and return a now-revoked record.
operations.error_outcome: Coarse consumer mapping returns Config, Cancelled, FeatureDisabled, or usually Broker. A blocking-closure panic is resumed on await, or propagates directly through inline spawn-failure fallback, and the caller's post-await local continuation is skipped. A buffered error can transfer to a later poll, and a concurrent slice can overwrite an unconsumed outcome before either caller observes it.
operations.timeout_rule: Caller timeout uses the attached Cx timer driver when present and wall_now otherwise; expiration is Ok(None), not an error. Every backend clamps Duration::as_nanos() to u64::MAX before Instant::saturating_add_nanos, so durations above u64::MAX nanoseconds share that effective horizon and Instant saturation can clamp it further. After the first iteration the deadline check can win while a completed slice outcome remains in the shared slot for another poll.
operations.cancellation_rule: Checked at entry and between slices; fallback-cap saturation yields without consulting this operation Cx, an in-flight blocking slice is not interrupted, and dropping the await does not stop an already-started closure. A slice writes shared buffered_outcome before its caller resumes, so cancellation can leave a record/error/snapshot for a later poll. On the real-broker auto-commit path the offset may already be stored. Deterministic poll has no auto-store step; each local scan synchronously holds consumer state and waits for the process-global broker mutex without observing Cx until control returns to the outer loop.
operations.shutdown_rule: Rejected when entered after close, but close, subscribe, rebalance, and seek do not clear buffered_outcome and the feature-on loop does not recheck open or a newer assignment epoch before consuming it. An in-flight broker poll can therefore apply a stale snapshot, repopulate local state, and return a record after close or revocation. Deterministic poll_cursor also survives membership changes and modulo-remaps onto the new sorted assignment set.
operations.resource_bound: Exactly one repository-local buffered_outcome slot is shared by all poll calls; concurrent slices can overwrite it and silently remove a record/error from application observation. Each deterministic poll attempt clones the complete unbounded BTree assignment set, including topic strings, into a Vec, may scan every assignment, and performs additional allocated topic-key lookups under the process-global broker mutex; this repeats after notifications. Record/topic/key/payload/header count and bytes plus native queues are not locally capped; max_poll_records is unused. The shared fallback counter caps successfully spawned blocking threads at 256 while excess callers wait; OS-thread spawn failure runs the blocking poll slice inline on the async worker.
operations.credential_payload_rule: Copies topic, key, payload, and headers, but missing payload becomes empty bytes and missing header value becomes empty bytes. Timestamp conversion collapses CreateTime versus LogAppendTime to Option<i64> milliseconds and maps their -1 values plus NotAvailable to None.

A blocking-closure panic is resumed on await, or propagates directly through inline spawn-failure fallback; because closed was already set, local clearing/notification are skipped and later close cannot retry. A concurrent second close can already have returned Ok while that first close is still pending or before it later fails, so its success is not cleanup evidence. Close also does not fence an already-admitted subscribe or poll: subscribe can re-subscribe the cleaned backend and return Config, while poll can consume its uncleared buffered outcome and return a record after close.

After closed swaps true, the first native cleanup has no later Cx check: fallback-cap saturation yields without consulting this operation Cx, unassign is not interrupted, and dropping the await either prevents backend cleanup from starting or discards an already-started closure's result. In both cases the post-await local map clearing and notification are skipped permanently, and every later close short-circuits.

routed_findings.finding: Workspace tests feature-unify test-internals through the conformance dev-dependency, so K0.1's default unit-test cfg-mismatch profile is not the effective workspace-test profile.

A downstream release build with test-internals can compile deterministic controls, but reaching deterministic broker storage panics outside test or debug_assertions; admission is not one uniform test-internals profile.
The insecure-transport bypass setter is callable in ordinary downstream debug builds because its cfg is test OR debug_assertions, not test-only.
KafkaProducer flush directly invokes a blocking native poll slice inside an async function and op_notify has no observer; close and flush are polling-based rather than wake-driven.

Producer or transaction-record cancellation after successful enqueue can return Cancelled while the broker record remains queued and the eventual callback is discarded; no typed delivery-certainty state exists. Transaction::send borrows rather than consumes its handle, so entry, backoff, or delivery cancellation leaves the shared phase Active and permits a later retry, commit, or abort.
Consumer poll converts null payload and null header values to empty byte vectors, losing incumbent wire distinctions.

On the real-broker path consumer auto commit stores the message offset before returning the record; commit before processing creates a loss window, while crash before delayed commit can redeliver. The default remains manual commit, and deterministic poll ignores the auto-commit field.

Consumer close marks closed before unsubscribe/unassign; concurrent close calls are not joined, so a second can return Ok while the first cleanup is pending or before it fails. Dropping the first close after that atomic swap can prevent backend cleanup or skip local clearing/notification after backend work, and later close cannot retry. An unassign error likewise leaves stale state. Close also does not fence admitted subscribe/poll work, allowing post-cleanup backend re-subscription or an uncleared buffered poll outcome to repopulate state and return after close.
Transaction commit and abort consume the handle, map most native failures to Broker, and use NeedsAbortRecovery without Fenced, Fatal, Ambiguous, or Closed public outcome states.
Transactional client configuration forces native idempotence true while config() can still report the caller's retained false value; deterministic transactions never deduplicate.
TLS key passwords are Debug-redacted but not zeroized, while SASL wrapper passwords are ZeroizeOnDrop; upstream authentication strings remain unsanitized.

Primary Kafka operations expose coarse string errors without stable ASUP-Exxx tokens or a complete metrics/tracing contract. Debug/test deterministic single-record sends use a case-sensitive critical-topic matcher and write an exact warning to stderr, while deterministic transaction batch commit bypasses that matcher and emits no per-topic warning. Release test-internals critical and noncritical sends use distinct panic diagnostics.

KafkaClient overlaps the primary consumer surface but exposes only a one-topic diagnostics trait; its no-feature backend descriptor says deterministic, crate tests can create the diagnostic DeterministicConsumer, and after successful topic validation every non-test consumer() call fails FeatureDisabled.
Producer payload checks omit key, headers, topic, framing, batch aggregate, and deterministic storage; consumer record/header copies and state maps also lack aggregate bounds.
ReadCommitted is only a native client setting and the deterministic path has no transaction/isolation model; static source cannot establish isolation correctness.
The parser-hook Compression From<u8> mapping uses modulo four and can never construct Zstd.

TransactionalProducer begin is not single-flight. Concurrent Idle calls can duplicate native initialization, and concurrent NeedsAbortRecovery calls can both abort, clobber an already-reactivated Active phase back to Idle, admit multiple transaction handles, or let a later failure leave Idle while a handle remains active. Duplicate live handles can both pass ensure-active before either marks Finalizing, allowing native commit, abort, or mixed finalization calls to execute; a separately checked native send can enqueue or complete during/after another handle's finalization, while deterministic send performs a second Active check and can reject instead. Deterministic loser Drop can poison the winner's Finalizing phase. Drop only poisons Active or Finalizing, so an unfinished handle dropped after the shared phase was clobbered to Idle does not repair the inconsistency.

All real-consumer polls share one buffered_outcome slot. Cancellation or deadline expiry can transfer a completed record/error/snapshot to a later poll, while concurrent slices can overwrite an unconsumed outcome and silently remove it from application observation after an auto-commit offset may already have been stored.

Real consumer operations always use the process-global fallback blocking-thread bridge; transaction operations prefer the configured Cx blocking pool and otherwise use that fallback. The pool caps worker concurrency but admits an uncapped pending SegQueue, can retain an accepted task indefinitely after worker-spawn failure with no live worker, skips queued work when its CancelOnDrop handle is dropped, and turns shutdown enqueue rejection into a bridge panic. The fallback caps successfully spawned threads at 256 but not waiting callers, saturation yields without consulting the operation Cx, dropping the await does not stop an already-started closure, and OS-thread spawn failure runs the broker closure inline on the async worker. Closure panics are resumed by either bridge or propagate directly through inline fallback.

Consumer broker effects are serialized only inside blocking closures; subscribe, rebalance, commit, and seek apply local continuations afterward without an ordering fence. Concurrent calls can therefore leave local state older than the backend. Poll can likewise apply an older buffered snapshot after a newer subscription, rebalance, or seek and return a revoked or old-topic record.

Native ClientConfig errors can carry the rejected configuration value. Producer, primary-consumer, and KafkaClient mappings expose that value without redaction through public error Display/Debug, so a rejected sasl.password or ssl.key.password can leak plaintext credentials.

The deterministic consumer poll cursor is not reset by subscribe, rebalance, or close. It persists across membership changes and is reduced modulo the new sorted assignment length, making the first partition after resubscription or reassignment depend on prior polling history.

TransactionalProducer begin marks shared phase Active before awaiting native begin and constructs the Transaction handle only afterward. Dropping or cancelling in that window can skip queued pool work or discard an executing/fallback result while stranding Active with no handle or Drop hook; later begin reports transaction already active and no public recovery path remains.
